findings.finding: CEO Liu Chang filed eleven Form 4s in eight weeks - 2026-07-06, 07-20, 07-22, 07-31, 08-03, 08-10, 08-11, 08-14, 08-24, 08-28 and 09-01 - taking her holding from 35,149 shares on 20 July to 92,786 on 1 September (a 164% increase) at prices between $1.89 and $2.46, with no sale anywhere in the index; the 9,216-share purchase on 2026-08-28 alone is 74% of the stock's 12,515-share twenty-day average volume.
findings.adversary_note: Two things put this in the middle-upper band rather than the low one, and the second is the stronger. First, it is published in the corpus, and published by a service whose entire purpose is to surface exactly this: ceo-buys.com posts reproducing every transaction with size, price and resulting holding appear in two separate stored bodies (docs/efbcfae7dffa7859bd8b63014428f3765f25ef93.txt and docs/eaf570aeb2ef6c8dc678cbc913a1e7dfceac5654.txt), on top of the Form 4 index itself. A dedicated insider-buying aggregator republishing each purchase within days is not an unpublished fact; it is a syndicated one, and the hunter's own independence field describes two sources carrying it. Second, and decisively, the purchases are already in the price bars because they ARE the price bars. On 12,515 shares of average daily volume, a buyer taking down clips worth up to 74% of a session is the marginal bid, and the tape shows exactly that: run_up_5d +6.05% and run_up_20d +13.43% into the print, in a $23m ADR with 95.8% realised volatility. The claim that the market has not priced the CEO's conviction is contradicted by the fact that the CEO's own buying moved the stock 13% in twenty sessions. What is left is the forward question of whether she keeps buying, which the corpus cannot answer. The hunter is right that the dollar size is trivial - roughly 57,600 shares at about $2.15, some $124k, or half a percent of market capitalisation - and I agree with it that the argument has to be about frequency rather than magnitude, which makes it a sentiment inference rather than a quantity.

findings.finding: Five Form 4s were filed in the five weeks before the annual print (2026-07-30 twice, 2026-08-13, 2026-08-21, 2026-08-26), continuing a documented open-market buying programme by the two Elsztain brothers (Chairman and CEO) and director Saul Zang who together bought the equivalent of ~120,000 ADS at $10.57-$11.23 between 2026-04-22 and 2026-06-05, and there is not a single Form 144 in the whole 400-day index.
findings.adversary_note: This fails on size before it fails on publication. The April-June buying the finding relies on is 120,000 ADS at $10.57-$11.23 - about $1.3m against a $796m market cap, or 0.17%, and roughly five days of the 245,980-share average volume. That is the error the brief says hunters make most often: real, low-visibility, and far too small to matter. The five Form 4s themselves are in filings.json with acceptance times (0001034957-26-000055 on 08-26, 0001654954-26-007786 on 08-21, 0001654954-26-007576 on 08-13, and two on 07-30), so they were reachable, but no body is stored and therefore no share count, no price and no reporting person is established anywhere in this capture - the claim that they continue the same family programme is an assumption, not a reading. I have a specific doubt about their provenance that the capture cannot resolve and that would void the finding if correct: Cresud is a foreign private issuer, it files 20-F and 6-K, and foreign private issuers are exempt from Section 16 reporting under Rule 3a12-3(b), so Form 4s indexed on this CIK are more likely Cresud appearing as a reporting owner in another issuer's Section 16 filing - Cresud is the controlling holder of IRSA and has other listed affiliates - than Argentine executives reporting purchases of CRESY ADS. Nothing in the capture tells me which it is. The April-June detail is in any case published, in the stored body at the 2026-06-10T16:14:13Z entry. And the closing argument - 'if this were priced the stock would not be trading at the chairman's May purchase price' - is a run-up inference: the stock is up 9.63% over twenty days and 42.4% off its 52-week low, so the tape has hardly ignored the name.

findings.finding: This is the fiscal-year-end release (year ended 30 June 2026) and at this company that is the release that carries the annual dividend proposal: the prior year distributed ARS 93,782m in cash plus IRSA shares, a stated ~8% yield, and the corpus records annual ADS distributions of $1.056 (2023) and $0.9921 (2024) with $0.50-1.00 expected this year against an $11.84 share price.
findings.adversary_note: The mechanism is structural and known, and the corpus publishes the parameters. That the fiscal-year-end release at this issuer carries the annual distribution is a fixed feature of Cresud's calendar, and the stored body already sets out the history and the expectation - ARS 93,782m plus IRSA shares last year at a stated ~8% yield, $1.056 per ADS in 2023, $0.9921 in 2024 and $0.50-1.00 anticipated this year (docs/967a6ce212eea3280a8162afd68eb43202019d07.txt, entries 2026-08-24T20:41:30Z, 2026-08-04T12:02:28Z, 2025-11-10T20:55:43Z, 2025-05-09T19:26:15Z). A known annual event with a published three-year history and a published expected range is not a hidden catalyst; it is a scheduled one, and 'everyone knows the distribution comes at the FY release' is the definition of age without novelty. The residual is genuine but narrow: the exact amount is unknown and is a function of ARS-denominated results, so there is real variance around a known event. That is worth something, which is why I am at 72 rather than 90. Two problems reduce it further. The argument that the issuer 'gets no US news coverage, no sell-side preview and no consensus in the whole capture' is an n_queries=0 artefact of a capture that ran no news search on this ticker, not a fact about coverage. And a dividend that transfers 4-8% of market cap out of the company is close to value-neutral to a holder on the ex-date, so the size the finding quotes is not the size of the price effect.

findings.finding: The company's own reported numbers cut against the bull case the corpus repeats: adjusted EBITDA was 39.7% lower year on year in fiscal Q1 2026 and 19.0% lower in the fiscal first half, with agribusiness contributing only ARS 15,350m of ARS 137,967m, while the headline net income swing (ARS 193,932m against a prior-year loss) is attributed explicitly to 'the gain from changes in the fair value of IRSA investment properties' - a non-cash mark.
findings.adversary_note: The finding says it itself: these are the company's own reported numbers, reproduced verbatim in the captured body from the Q1 FY26 and H1 FY26 releases (docs/967a6ce212eea3280a8162afd68eb43202019d07.txt, entries 2026-02-10T14:35:44Z and 2025-11-10T20:54:23Z). Company-disclosed prior-period results are the top of the priced-in scale, and there is no arithmetic here that the releases did not already perform - the -39.7% Q1 and -19.0% H1 adjusted EBITDA figures and the attribution of the net-income swing to the IRSA fair-value mark are the company's own words. The mechanism also does not reach this print as news: these are periods already reported and already reacted to, and the whole point of a fiscal-year-end release is that it supersedes them. What is actually being claimed is a narrative gap - that the corpus's other 76 items talk about record crops while operating earnings contract - and a divergence between retail chatter and a filing is not an unpriced fact, it is an observation about the composition of a Stocktwits dump. To the hunter's credit this finding is signed against its own two positive findings and labelled as the reason the net number is low, which is the right instinct.

findings.finding: Alternative data shows Samsara accelerating hiring into the print: LinkedIn headcount up 4.0% over three months to 5,745 (against 2,895 in the most recent official filings) with 262 active job postings - and AltIndex's own framing is that headcount leads revenue, companies hiring before acceleration and cutting before disappointment.
findings.adversary_note: The page is public and the capture holds it: altindex.com/ticker/iot/employees-linkedin is a free, indexed web page, stored at docs/71fcfd6ecce3406e232cc422335b088aa655d78c.txt and captured at 2026-09-03T15:16Z, hours before an after-the-close release. Alt-data headcount series are also among the most widely purchased inputs on the buy side, so 'never carried by a wire' is not the same as unavailable to the marginal price-setter. More decisive is the internal weakness: the finding reports LinkedIn headcount of 5,745 against 2,895 in the company's filings, a factor of two, which is an admission that the series is not measuring the same population as the payroll - it picks up contractors, stale profiles and mis-tagged accounts - so a 4.0% three-month change in it cannot support a claim about hiring. And the direction is not obvious even if the number were clean: 4.0% over three months annualises to roughly 17% headcount growth at a company reporting revenue growth in the low thirties, which is as easily read as hiring decelerating relative to revenue. The mechanism cited ('headcount leads revenue') is AltIndex's own product marketing, quoted from the page. Finally, the corroboration is published wire copy that states the conclusion outright - marketscreener carrying RBC calling the raised FY27 guide 'somewhat conservative' - so the beatable-guide thesis is in the captured coverage, not missing from it. The closing appeal, 'if it were priced the stock would not have fallen 7.5% in five sessions', is run-up-as-evidence and is answered by the finding's own #2.

findings.finding: Samsara Beyond 2026, the company's customer conference, ran on 24-25 June 2026 with a broad wave of AI-for-physical-operations product announcements - i.e. squarely inside the fiscal second quarter now being reported, so the bookings and pipeline effect of that launch cycle lands in this print and in the guide that follows it.
findings.adversary_note: The conference and its announcements are published twice over in this capture - the third-party write-up at docs/b0905a53065825f9d085b78d52ee2f2e472e46b3.txt with datePublished 2026-06-24/25, and the company's own announcement blog captured as a separate item in the same sweep - and the finding concedes the launches 'are priced as news'. What it claims instead is that the market has not noticed the conference fell inside the quarter being reported. That cannot be right: fiscal period ends are public, the conference date was public, and every analyst modelling a July-quarter ARR number is modelling a period that contains 24-25 June. There is no hidden calendar here. The mechanism is also slow relative to the claim: in a land-and-expand telematics model, product announcements at a customer conference convert to net-new ARR over multiple quarters through pilots and renewals, so five weeks of a mid-quarter launch wave is not where the bookings show up. And the supporting observation - '+1.4% over twenty sessions, so nothing was paid for it' - measures the twenty sessions ending in September, more than two months after the conference, which is the wrong window for the inference and is in any case the baseline's run_up_20d field.

findings.finding: The five-session -7.45% fall into the print is sector, not company: the same sweep captures a piece arguing 'The SaaS Rout of 2026 Is Even Worse Than You Think - for the first time ever software now trades at a discount to the S&P 500', and the last Samsara print (2026-06-04) fell 1.16% despite 31% revenue growth, a raised FY27 guide to $2.013bn and a third consecutive GAAP profit.
findings.adversary_note: The hunter grades this correctly itself: it is a framing argument, not a datapoint, and it cuts both ways. Both supporting documents are published and captured pre-print (docs/8bffde25efcdb9f843be18df8d4b6d118901b98c.txt and docs/2f8b846022e979ea21d45787ca3bb1f9eb24b711.txt, items 17 and 22 of the 09-03 15:16Z sweep), and the saastr piece's entire thesis - software at a discount to the S&P for the first time - is a widely circulated sector observation, i.e. exactly the consensus narrative rather than a gap in it. The last print's outcome (-1.16% on 31% growth, a raised FY27 guide to $2.013bn and a third GAAP profit) is company-disclosed and sits in the baseline history. What is left is the assertion that the -7.45% five-day run-in is sector multiple compression rather than informed selling, which is an interpretation of the baseline's own run_up_5d field and is the precise argument I am instructed not to accept as a substitute for an option reading. And here I do have the option reading, and it does not support a positioning story: the 11.55% implied move for the 09-04 expiry is a fraction above the 11.08% median, which is a market pricing ordinary event risk, not a market that has crowded onto one side. The JPMorgan sector report is cited without a figure extracted, so it corroborates nothing.

findings.finding: The 25% slide from $12.05 on 2026-06-30 to $9.05 at the print coincides exactly with a supply event nobody has connected: an S-3 filed 2026-07-02 and declared effective 2026-07-16 (form EFFECT accepted 2026-07-17T04:15:26Z), with Rule 144 notices of intended sale on 2026-07-09 and 2026-07-10 and a Form 4 on 2026-07-13 in between - and then no filing of any kind for the seven weeks into the print.
findings.adversary_note: The finding is internally at war with itself. If the shelf and the 144 notices caused the 25% slide, then the supply has already been absorbed by the tape and the effect is in the price - which is the strongest form of 'already priced' available to me; if they did not cause it, the coincidence of dates is the whole argument and there is nothing left. The hunter cannot have both 'coincides exactly with a supply event' and 'nobody has connected it'. All five accessions are in filings.json with acceptance times - the S-3 0001437749-26-022501 on 2026-07-02, the EFFECT 9999999995-26-002338 on 2026-07-17, the two 144s on 07-09 and 07-10, the Form 4 on 07-13 - so the sequence was reachable to any EDGAR reader eight weeks ahead, which is the reachable-but-unconnected band, and the corpus stores no body for any of them, so no size is established for the shelf or the notices. The mechanism also does not reach forward: the finding itself notes no filing of any kind in the seven weeks into the print, and the baseline shows run_up_20d of only -6.51% against the 25% peak-to-print decline, so the July supply pressure is spent and the recent tape is quiet. What remains is the interpretive claim that the drawdown was technical rather than fundamental and therefore reverses on a decent print - an assertion about the reason for a price move, made from the price move, with no dated source. The 10-K risk-factor language about concentrated-holder selling is boilerplate that appears in the risk factors of essentially every sponsor-backed issuer and cannot corroborate a specific July sale.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide the company raised on 2026-06-04 - revenue $410-425m, adjusted EBITDA $98-105m, free cash flow at least $45m, driven by data centre and infrastructure volume - implies a materially stronger second half than the $90.6m Q1 and $106.8m Q2 already reported, and this print is the seasonally strongest quarter, the same quarter that produced a +12.19% reaction in 2025.
findings.adversary_note: This restates published guidance and then does the arithmetic backwards. The FY26 raise - revenue $410-425m, adjusted EBITDA $98-105m, FCF at least $45m - was in the 2026-06-04 release, is in the captured Stocktwits body at the 2026-06-04T20:18:01Z entry (docs/b56e9371bd04e596d5a459214b6f5deabf719b47.txt), and the market repriced it violently and immediately: the baseline's own history records +30.70% on that print, the largest reaction in the seven-event set. Guidance that produced a 31% up-move is the definition of priced. The 'unaggregated arithmetic' is also weaker than claimed and arguably points the other way. Against $197.4m reported in H1, the $410-425m range requires $213-228m in H2, which is only 8-15% above H1 - and for an October fiscal year end, H2 is the seasonally strong half containing the summer construction season, so a mid-single-digit to low-teens sequential half-on-half step is the ordinary seasonal shape rather than a stretch. Presenting that as tension misreads the seasonality the finding elsewhere relies on. Finally, the citation is mismatched: source_date is 2026-06-04 but the source URL is the 2026-03-10 Q1 FY26 release, so the document being cited is not the document containing the raise.

findings.finding: Insider selling stopped completely seven months before the print: Form 144 / Form 4 pairs were filed on a monthly cadence through the prior winter (144s on 2025-11-03, 2025-12-01, 2025-12-04, 2026-01-02, 2026-02-02, with matching Form 4s on 2025-11-05, 2025-12-03, 2025-12-08, 2026-01-06, 2026-02-04) and then there is not a single Form 4, Form 144 or 8-K of any kind after 2026-05-14 in the entire 400-day index.
findings.adversary_note: I will not score this high, because an absence genuinely cannot be published and nothing in the capture draws it out - but I will not score it low either, because it is close to information-free and the hunter half says so. The whole EDGAR index is in filings.json, so the gap after 2026-02-04 is reachable by anyone who lists the filings, which is the 20-40 band. What makes it weak is that the finding's own alternative explanation is the likely one: a Rule 10b5-1 plan that ran monthly from November to February and then stopped is what an expiring twelve-month plan looks like, and no replacement plan is required to be announced. The claim also has no size at all - not one share count or dollar value for any of the five 144/Form 4 pairs is stored - so even read as a signal it is a signal of unknown magnitude at a $205m issuer. And the buyback corroboration undercuts rather than supports it: if the company's May guidance already pointed publicly to 'potential for renewed share buybacks as cash generation exceeds expectations' with $80.5m of cash and no debt, then the capital-return story is published (seekingalpha, 2026-05-23) and the insider-selling halt adds nothing to it. Finally, the argument that the halt cannot be priced because the stock fell 54% from its high across the same window is run-up-as-evidence and would prove the opposite just as easily.

findings.finding: Between 2026-06-25 and 2026-08-16 the company put out an unbroken run of AI-knowledge proof points - a new AI agent for Zoom Contact Center (06-25), a joint Deloitte report on the '$9 trillion knowledge crisis' (06-22), Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader status for customer service knowledge management (07-21), a named enterprise win at Unigarant (08-11), two Stevie Awards (08-12/13) and a company statement on AI knowledge ARR (08-16) - into a fiscal-year-end print at which the AI Knowledge Hub ARR mix is the disclosed metric.
findings.adversary_note: Six company press releases in eight weeks is the opposite of unpublished. Every item the finding lists - the Zoom Contact Center agent (06-25), the Deloitte knowledge-crisis report (06-22), Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader (07-21), the Unigarant win (08-11), the Stevie Awards (08-12/13) and the AI knowledge ARR statement (08-16) - is a company-issued announcement, at least two of them carried by Yahoo Finance (the 08-16 ARR piece and the Unigarant piece are both cited to finance.yahoo.com), and all of them reach me through the stored body docs/d429dbeec7ed4ef9374b66c21148a175c38c3ac2.txt. Company-issued proof points distributed on a wire and then indexed in a captured stream are the 70-85 band by construction. What the finding actually observes is that the market did not care - and it quotes the reason from its own corpus: '7% revenue growth for a company selling AI agents is terrible' and 'growth here absolutely sucks'. A market that has read the announcements and decided the consolidated growth rate matters more than the mix is a market that has priced them, not one that has missed them. The Gartner Leader argument is the strongest residual - recognition in a category can lengthen or shorten enterprise cycles - but that effect shows up in bookings over several quarters, not in a fiscal-year-end print six weeks later, and the finding offers no ARR figure, no dollar value for Unigarant and no growth-rate delta, so there is no magnitude to weigh against the disappointing headline growth the market is already looking at.

findings.finding: An independent photonics research note dated 2026-07-19 documents exactly why Ciena's last print was sold: on 2026-06-04 the company reported revenue up 40%, adjusted EPS nearly quadrupled and RAISED its full-year guide, beat consensus with no guidance cut and no ugly headline, and the stock still fell 13.7% that day and 8.9% the next - 'the results were not the problem', it was the expectations stacked in front of the price; Ciena has since fallen from a 2026-06-02 peak close of $627.00 to $354.16 the night before this print, a 43.5% de-rating of that same expectation stack.
findings.adversary_note: Every component of this is either published in the admissible corpus or already the level. The note itself is stored (docs/d8fad12136d81c02b77cfcbd69e21b0145c1d1ec.txt) and indexed in snapshots/20260902T152400Z.json, which clean-view lists as admissible - so its thesis was publicly readable six weeks before the print. The facts it interprets are the most heavily reported events in this name's year: the 2026-06-04 beat-and-raise and the 13.7% sell-off are in the baseline history as -13.66%, and the 43.5% de-rating from the 06-02 peak is the baseline's own pct_from_52w_high of -43.52%. That leaves only the interpretation - 'the results were not the problem, the expectation stack was' - and an interpretation of a completed 43% de-rating is not a new fact about the coming quarter; it is a restatement of the price. This is also the argument I am specifically instructed not to accept in reverse, so I will not accept it forward either: 'the stock has fallen a long way, therefore the setup is asymmetric' is the run-up doing duty for a distribution, and it is undated. The supporting option argument is now checkable and it cuts against the finding rather than for it. A real, pre-print implied move exists in the admissible sweep: 'Ciena options suggest 9.4% stock move after earnings release' appears as a title in search_trace/20260902T152400Z.json, and a Benzinga 'Broadcom Week: 10 Stocks Set For Double-Digit Moves' piece is indexed in the same admissible snapshot. A 9.4% implied move on a 12.9% historical median is not the market ignoring positioning risk; it is the market pricing a large move and pricing it slightly below a median that is itself dominated by two outliers. Contamination note, since I am the independent check here: every document this finding cites is in a clean-view-admissible snapshot and is dated before the print, and the chain from the 07-19 note plus the -43.5% de-rating to a bullish tilt is fully reconstructible without knowing the outcome - so I find no sign of answer-aiming in its construction, only in its confidence.

findings.finding: The optical supply chain that gates Ciena's shipments reported strongly in the quarter Ciena is about to report: Lumentum rocketed 15% on blowout earnings, Coherent climbed 9% and Corning gained 5%, with a 2026-08-13 piece framing 'the insane opportunity for companies like Marvell and Ciena' - while Ciena itself fell 40%+ over the same window.
findings.adversary_note: The peer prints are wire copy and the capture proves it: the 247wallst piece is stored (docs/6296a9060a16aa4bf2c677d8280dc87087871301.txt and docs/6ea0bf5261db51c3cffe7577364a0efc68173223.txt) and indexed as items 23 and 24 of snapshots/20260902T152400Z.json, which clean-view admits, and its headline explicitly names Ciena. So an article whose thesis is 'the insane opportunity for companies like Marvell and Ciena' was in the public news stream three weeks before the print - that is not an unaggregated divergence, that is the aggregation. Lumentum's 15%, Coherent's 9% and Corning's 5% were each their own headline event on their own day, and the fact that Ciena fell while they rose is the price bars, which is where I am told to look first: the market saw the supplier results and sold Ciena anyway, which is the market's answer to the read-through, not its absence. The mechanism is also genuinely two-sided in a way the finding half-concedes: Lumentum and Coherent are Ciena's upstream vendors, so record component demand and record component pricing are as easily a gross-margin headwind for the systems buyer as a volume tailwind, and the corpus contains an item taking the opposite view of the same complex ('Optics Stocks Divide'). Its own independence field says the range crosses zero, which is the correct read and is close to saying there is no edge here.

findings.finding: A dense insider-selling cluster sits at the top of the August bounce: four Form 4s on 2026-08-18 (the session the stock fell from $445.18 to $405.54), Rule 144 notices on 2026-08-14 and twice on 2026-08-17, four more 144s on 2026-07-15, and four Form 4s on 2026-07-17, plus a further Form 4 on 2026-09-02, the day before the print.
findings.adversary_note: The finding concedes the point and the corpus confirms it: a captured item is titled 'Is Ciena's Recent Surge Sustainable Amidst Insider Selling' (kavout, 2026-08-18) and Nasdaq's insider-activity page for CIEN is captured in the same sweep, so the insider-selling story is published, aggregated and headlined in this capture - the 70-85 band by definition. The residual is timing rather than fact, and the timing argument does not survive contact with the mechanics: the densest Form 4 day coinciding with a 9% down session is what 10b5-1 plan sales look like when they are pooled on a scheduled window, and the 09-02 Form 4 is a single filing with no size in the capture. Against a $56.6bn market cap and 2.0m shares a day of turnover, executive sales would have to be extraordinary to matter, and no share count or dollar value for any Form 4 or 144 is stored, so the magnitude is not merely small - it is absent. Note too that a Form 4 reports a transaction that has already happened, so the supply it describes is behind the tape rather than in front of it.

findings.finding: American Century's 13F filed 2026-08-12 raised its Planet Labs position from 5,813,758 to 14,399,902 shares - a 148% increase of 8.6m shares - making it a top-five institutional owner, disclosed in the middle of a drawdown that has taken the stock 64.3% below its 52-week high.
findings.adversary_note: Three things put this well up the scale, and the hunter concedes the most important one. First, it is published in the corpus: the position change is reported in the stored Stocktwits body at the 2026-08-28T20:57:39Z entry (docs/9d6320246d8c47c15bc0b33e8312f82c2fb4986e.txt), so it was circulating in the retail stream six days before the print - the finding's own quote, 'while retail is running scared, institutions keep accumulating', is that circulation. Second, 13F holdings are a quarterly public dataset that dozens of free trackers parse and republish within hours of filing; a top-five holder doubling a position is exactly the change those services headline. Third, and decisively, the hunter states the disqualifying caveat itself: a 13F filed 2026-08-12 reports positions as of 30 June, so this is a fact about Q2 ownership disclosed six weeks late and says nothing about flow into the print - and the tape since then is -19.23% over twenty sessions and -13.28% over five, which is what it looks like when whoever owns the stock is not defending it. Ownership composition is also not a directional claim about a quarter's results; it changes who reacts, not what is reported. The small 9/18 call buyer noted as corroboration is one retail options observation with no size.

findings.finding: The corpus attributes the space-complex de-rating to a capital-flow event rather than to Planet's fundamentals: participants describe 'the volatility before spacex' and 'the pumpers that disappeared after the spacex ipo', and the drawdown moved in lockstep with RKLB across the same sessions, with the stock printing '10 of last 11 days red' and volume described repeatedly as unusually low.
findings.adversary_note: This is an interpretation of the drawdown built from the drawdown, plus retail commentary that is itself in the capture. Every element is published in the same stored body - 'the volatility before spacex', 'the pumpers that disappeared after the spacex ipo', '10 of last 11 days red' - so the capital-rotation narrative is not missing from the observed corpus, it is the observed corpus. The RKLB lockstep is likewise computed from two public price series that anyone can overlay, and the SpaceX listing is one of the most heavily covered market events imaginable; a sector rotation into a newly listed giant is structural and known, not a hidden mechanism. The load-bearing inference - 'if the market were pricing a Planet-specific deterioration there would be a filing, a downgrade or a contract loss to point at, and the filing record is empty' - is an argument from the absence of evidence in a capture that contains no news search at all, which is precisely the reasoning the instructions rule out. Markets de-rate on estimate drift, macro and sector multiple compression without any of those three artefacts. And the 'unusually low volume' claim sits oddly against avg_volume_20d of 6.49m shares in a $7.5bn name. I also have to flag that the cited source URL for this finding is a European public-procurement notice (ted.europa.eu), which has no bearing on any assertion in it - the actual evidence is the Stocktwits body.

The guidance suspension, the Section 232 amendment mechanics and the 'in excess of $500M for the remainder of the year, before any mitigation measures' figure all come from the 2026-04-15 release and sit in docs/07166c5ce4d72f772ffef77207bc045b50a8ec47.txt, indexed in snapshots/20260830T084024Z.json item 1 (admissible per clean-view), at entries dated 2026-04-15. So the market has already run this exact test once, in public, and the answer was mitigation. Age is not novelty. The genuinely useful part of this finding is not an unpriced fact at all but a correction to the baseline: the 2.19% median is computed from six 6-Ks matched by text on a 36-day inferred cadence, which the baseline itself flags as cadence_implausible, so the expected move for a real quarterly print is materially wider. That is a measurement critique, not an edge, and it cuts both ways. I also reject the supporting inference - 'the market has quietly assumed the $500M is largely mitigable because the stock is only 22.5% off its high' - as run-up-as-evidence, and note it is self-undermining: if the market has assumed mitigation, then the market has taken a view, which is pricing.

findings.finding: An 8-K with items 1.01, 8.01 and 9.01 - a material definitive agreement plus other events - was filed on 2026-07-01, the day after the offering closed, and its contents appear nowhere in the 57-item capture; nine weeks later the retail base is still 'waiting for the big news on the company's next acquisitions'.

An 8-K carrying items 1.01, 8.01 and 9.01 filed on 2026-07-01, the day after a marketed secondary closed, is the textbook filing for the underwriting agreement itself: the underwriting agreement is a material definitive agreement (1.01), the closing or pricing press release goes under 8.01, and the agreement plus opinion are the 9.01 exhibits. That reading explains the item combination, the date and the absence of any coverage far better than an unannounced acquisition, and if it is right the filing is a mechanical adjunct to an event that is already fully published - which is why I put this at the midpoint rather than in the reachable-but-unconnected band. The finding's alternative readings do not help it either: a credit facility signed alongside a raise is routine and a purchase agreement would have been announced, because a company that raised $100m explicitly to fund acquisitions has every incentive to disclose one and the retail base is on record nine weeks later still waiting. The hunter concedes the direction is uncertain and that this collapses into #0's source cluster. What keeps me from going higher is honest: the body is not stored, so I cannot prove my reading, and the corpus cannot resolve it either way.

Short interest is published on a semi-monthly schedule by the exchanges and consumed by every systematic desk, and the hunter concedes the level is priced; the analyst marks are published too - the JPMorgan raise from $20 to $22 is in the admissible body at the 2026-08-18T15:05:20Z entry and the UBS raise-with-a-sell at 2026-08-20T11:57:53Z (docs/ca6d43739e452eaab3dbc22324f4ec33cc9535f0.txt, snapshots/20260830T084020Z.json, allowed by clean-view). So all three inputs are public. The residual is the assembly - crowded short plus below-market targets plus a fiscal-year-end guide equals forced target raises - and that is a squeeze mechanic, which is the most widely traded structural feature in equities and is neither new nor company-specific. The bigger problem is provenance. I read the body: the only support for the short-interest magnitude is a single retail post, '$CPB short interest in CPB is 20% of available float. Watching to see if this squeezes' (2026-08-19T19:37:37Z), plus an '8-9 days to cover' remark from 2026-07-16. There is no FINRA or exchange figure anywhere in this capture, and 20-24% of float in a $6.9bn consumer staple is a large claim resting on a forum assertion - so the magnitude that does all the work is unverifiable here, which is the 45-65 band. The corpus also contains the mechanism already operating and being publicly narrated ('the small squeeze is over with. Drift back under 22, then another mini squeeze and repeat till most of the short interest is churned through', 2026-08-20), i.e. participants have watched two squeezes complete before this print. Citation hygiene: the source URL given is a finviz story about a new soup lineup, which supports none of the claim's assertions. On contamination, which is my specific charge here: the CPB brief files a bullish squeeze finding and a bearish dividend-cut finding and explicitly signs them against each other and asks the scorer to collapse them. That is the shape of a hunter that does not know the answer. I find no evidence of answer-aiming in either CPB finding.

No dated source in the capture says that, and it is precisely the shape of argument the instructions warn about - reading the run-up, here the fade, and asserting a distributional consequence. Two further weaknesses: the claim's own price path is mis-specified - there were two distinct pops, 06-30 and 07-31, not one - and a takeover-floor argument is a claim about the shape of the reaction rather than its direction, so it cannot rank this name against others on a signed scale.

findings.finding: A National Firearms Act change surfaced around 2026-08-13 that participants read as freeing short-barrelled rifles and shotguns ('they better be cranking up the production lines for short barrel rifles and shotguns. findings.adversary_note: A federal change to National Firearms Act treatment of short-barrelled rifles and shotguns, and national concealed-carry legislation, are not obscure trade items - they are front-page political news, and if they happened around 2026-08-13 every holder of a firearms manufacturer knew within hours. The capture confirms circulation rather than absence: the discussion is in the stored body at the 08-13 and 08-14 entries, and so is the market's verdict, at 2026-08-18T14:21:47Z - 'the market isn't buying the gun hype' (docs/ea71a201cf07947ca72fac3a7a28ddabf6257f2a.txt). The finding then uses that verdict as its evidence, which is circular: 'the price is the evidence' cuts against a finding, not for it, because a 15.7% de-rating through the news window is the market pricing the news and rejecting the demand story. There is also a hard mechanism problem. This print covers the quarter ended 31 July 2026, and the regulatory change surfaced on 13 August - after the quarter closed. It cannot appear in a single reported number; at most it appears in forward commentary, and any order response to an expanded SBR market takes several quarters of production and channel fill. The hunter's own corroboration is a retail newsletter adding to a 'small-cap loser', which is a value trade, not confirmation of a demand signal. The absence of NICS or ATF data in the capture is an n_queries=0 artefact; those series are public monthly releases that every firearms analyst tracks.

findings.finding: Hello Group's ADS count has fallen from 206.1m to 147.7m over five years - a 28% reduction - while net cash per ADS has risen from $2.75 in 2021 to $8.16, against a pre-print share price of $5.485, i.e. the equity trades at about 67% of its net cash with the operating business valued at less than nothing.
findings.adversary_note: The arithmetic is published in the corpus, in the document the finding cites, by an author who performed it. docs/7d6c6390a190e13da2e63cfdd83fc28c1f302e2e.txt carries the 2026-06-02 entry setting out the ADS count falling from 206.1m to 147.7m, net cash per ADS rising from $2.75 to $8.16, and the resulting sub-net-cash valuation - so the calculation the finding presents as unaggregated is verbatim in the stored body, dated three months before the print. The inputs are also all company filings: share count and net cash come from the 20-F and the quarterly releases. Beyond publication, this is the archetype of structural and known: a China ADR trading below net cash with the operating business at a negative implied value is the defining feature of that entire cohort and has been for years, driven by discount-rate, governance and repatriation concerns that a quarterly print does not resolve. Age is not novelty, and a buyback mechanically lifting per-share cash every quarter is the most predictable thing in the story - it is disclosed, it is ongoing, and its arithmetic can be extrapolated by anyone. The 'I don't know if the market realized' quote is an author's rhetorical hedge, not evidence of non-publication, and the corroborating post about holding 'until $10 or the Spring dividend' shows the capital-return pattern is common knowledge in the holder base.

findings.finding: VersaBank filed Form 425 business-combination communications on 2026-07-28, 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-25, each paired with a 6-K the same day or the day before, and distributed a notice of meeting and proxy materials to shareholders on 2026-08-24 - i.e. a securities-registered transaction requiring a shareholder vote is live across the entire run-in to this print.
findings.adversary_note: The characterisation of Form 425 as 'the least-read filing type there is' inverts what the form actually is. A Form 425 is a filing OF a public communication about a business combination - a press release, an investor presentation, a shareholder letter - made under Rule 425 precisely because the issuer has already disseminated it publicly. Filing one is evidence of broad publication, not of obscurity. And the finding's own second piece of evidence is stronger still: a notice of meeting and proxy materials distributed to shareholders on 2026-08-24 is the most widely delivered document a company produces, sent to every holder of record. So a registered transaction requiring a shareholder vote is not a hidden fact in this name; it is the fact every holder has been mailed. That this capture contains no news coverage of it reflects n_queries=0 and a three-message social stream, which is a capture artefact I am instructed not to read as a concession. Where the finding is right, and genuinely useful, is on magnitude rather than direction - and the tape already says it. The baseline's eight matched events have a median absolute move of 0.82% and a maximum of 1.53%, run_up_20d is -0.41% and run_up_5d -2.68% with realised_vol_20d of 30.9%: this is a stock whose price is being set by exchange terms, exactly as the finding argues, and that compression is visible in the bars rather than waiting to be discovered. A magnitude observation that the baseline already encodes cannot be an edge, though it correctly warns against ranking this name on the median.

WLY gained on the day. The market saw the announcement, marked the stock up for it, and moved on - which is the plainest possible case of a fact being priced on the date it became known. The item is also published: it is in the admissible stored body at docs/d7ff82564a557ffced5d936a6aa2bd1f37a02219.txt, entry dated 2026-07-22T17:19:31Z, in snapshot 20260830T084039Z, and it concerns a named $5bn federal programme whose awards were a national news story covered across the AI and government-contracting press. A programme of that size and profile does not go unnoticed because a Stocktwits stream has 97 watchers. There is also a measurement error doing real work here. The finding argues 'if the market had paid for it, the twenty-session run-in would not be negative' - but the twenty sessions ending 2026-09-02 begin in early August, roughly a fortnight AFTER 22 July, so the window it cites does not contain the event it is testing. The -6.26% tells us nothing about how 22 July was received; the headline does, and it says the stock rose. Finally, the finding's own independence field concedes that nothing else in the capture points the same way.

findings.adversary_note: Reachable but unconnected, and probably empty. All of it is in filings.json with dates - the 8-K items 5.02/9.01 on 2026-07-09, the Form 3 on 07-17, seven Form 4s on 07-24 and a 144 on 07-02 - so an EDGAR reader had the sequence eight weeks out; no body is stored and nothing in the capture draws it together, which is why I score it in the low thirties rather than either extreme. But the pattern reads mundanely. Item 9.01 means an exhibit was attached, i.e. the change was announced by press release, so it was publicly disseminated at the time. Seven Form 4s filed on a single day is the signature of a scheduled grant or vesting event applying to a whole officer group, not seven new arrivals; the count of genuinely new insiders is one, the Form 3 filer. And a single Form 144 the week before proves nothing without a share count, which the capture does not have. The finding's mechanism - a first print under new leadership is where guidance gets rebased - is a generic heuristic with no size and an unstable sign, and the hunter signs it against its own main finding, which is the right instinct.

Then there is the class-B argument, which I think defeats the finding rather than rescuing it. The hunter says the class B stays unpriced because 'at 247 shares a day the class B does not reprice on information until someone needs to trade it'. That is true and it is precisely why this cannot be an edge: the baseline shows a median absolute print reaction of 1.98% with two recorded readings of exactly 0.00%, a deadband floored at 1.5%, and avg_volume_20d of 247 shares. A share class that does not move on its own earnings, on volume of a few hundred shares, cannot express a re-rating; a claim that information is unpriced in an instrument that cannot price anything is a statement about market structure, not an edge, and it is structural and known to anyone who has looked at the quote. Any ranking of WLYB on this basis is a ranking of an untradeable series.

findings.finding: Second-quarter revenue was already released on 2026-07-23 (a 6-K, recorded in the corpus as a 'Q2 26 Earnings Results & Recap' with a -0.5% reaction), so the 2026-09-03 release - two 6-Ks the same morning - carries the half-year profit-and-loss, margins and any outlook rather than the top line; the revenue surprise, which is what usually moves a luxury name, is already in the price.
findings.adversary_note: The finding's own sentence concedes it: 'the split-release structure (revenue in July, full accounts in September) is standard for European issuers'. Standard practice, followed by this issuer at every reporting cycle, is the definition of structural and known - every holder of a European luxury name knows the top line comes first and the margins come with the half-year accounts, and the baseline's median reaction of 1.75% across eight matched events is the market's long-standing acknowledgement of exactly that. The July revenue release is also published and captured: a 6-K dated 2026-07-23 in filings.json and a 'Q2 26 Earnings Results & Recap' entry in the admissible stored body (docs/43f565083d963dd453a2e5a3a2e636882ad642e2.txt, entry 2026-07-23T11:59:21Z), and the baseline records the reaction to it as -0.5%. So the claim that 'the revenue surprise is already in the price' is correct and is the opposite of an edge - it is an argument that this print carries less information than a normal one. What is offered as the unpriced residual, that the whole surprise now sits in gross margin and operating leverage, is a statement about which line to watch, not a view on what that line will say, and it has no size and no sign. The supporting point that 'no consensus anywhere in the capture' anchors a margin expectation is an n_queries=0 artefact; European luxury is among the most heavily covered sectors in the market and a margin consensus certainly exists outside this capture.

findings.finding: The stock fell 17.4% over twenty sessions and 8.5% over the last five into the print, on 848,200 shares a day, with no filing after a 6-K on 2026-08-24 and a passive 13G/A on 2026-08-12, no insider activity since 2026-05-11, and an admissible social stream containing exactly one message in the six weeks before the event.
findings.adversary_note: This is a claim built entirely from the baseline's own run-up fields and then read as evidence that something is unpriced, which inverts the logic. run_up_20d of -17.42% and run_up_5d of -8.52% are the market pricing something; calling the move 'unexplained' because this capture holds no company filing after 2026-08-24 and one social message in six weeks is an argument from the absence of evidence in a corpus with no news search at all. The stated principle - 'unexplained moves into a print are more often information than noise' - carries no source and is not testable here. There is also a quantitative problem that I think is decisive. This issuer's eight matched releases have a median absolute reaction of 1.75% and a maximum of 5.30%, against a 17.4% pre-print drift. A name whose price moves ten times more between prints than on them is not one where print information is the driver, so attributing a 17% drift to anticipation of a release that historically moves the stock under two percent is a mismatch of an order of magnitude. The hunter's own alternative - a coincident consumer-discretionary and luxury de-rating, evidenced from the LULU capture in this same run - is both more parsimonious and better supported, and it is why the finding is correctly kept small.

findings.finding: At the last print Quanex reported GAAP EPS of $0.07, down 84.1% year on year, on revenue of $462.4m up only 2.19%, and committed to 'recover price versus cost imbalance shortfall during the second half of the year, ASSUMING normal seasonality and subsiding inflation, while prioritizing debt repayment and opportunistic share repurchases' - so this release is the first of the two quarters that promise depends on, and the stock fell 13.42% on the day the promise was made.
findings.adversary_note: This restates published guidance and the market has already paid for it once, violently. The EPS of $0.07 down 84.1%, the $462.4m revenue up 2.19% and the price/cost recovery commitment - including its explicit conditionality on 'normal seasonality and subsiding inflation' - are all the company's own words from the 2026-06-04 release, and they are in the stored body at docs/a220e3377c889df309423af49d6f99e2300d27de.txt at the 2026-06-05 entries. The baseline records the market's response as -13.42%, the largest reaction in the seven-event set: the conditionality was read and discounted on the day. The finding's residual is that 'nobody in the observed corpus has checked the conditions', which is an n_queries=0 statement about a capture whose entire non-filing corpus is one Stocktwits thread - it is a fact about the sweep, not about whether building-products analysts have been tracking resin, aluminium and vinyl costs and US window shipments, which they do continuously. Worse for the finding, its own independence citation publishes the very framing it claims is missing: a same-day analytic item stating 'downside fades if inflation subsides, second-half price/cost recovery lands, and normal seasonality returns'. That is the conditional structure, itemised, in the capture. What is genuinely left is that this print is the first observation of a two-quarter promise - which is the calendar, known to everyone, and equally capable of resolving up.

findings.finding: Google shipped native e-signature into Workspace in the second half of August and followed it with a Google Cloud AI release that knocked DOCU and Thomson Reuters down more than 3% on 2026-08-26 - a direct attack on DocuSign's core product, arriving three weeks before the print, and the stock absorbed it and closed 15.9% higher over the twenty sessions anyway.
findings.adversary_note: The finding refutes itself in its own sentence: 'the stock absorbed it and closed 15.9% higher over the twenty sessions anyway.' That is the market considering the Google threat and declining to reprice DocuSign for it, which is the strongest form of already-priced available to me. The events are also wire copy stored in this capture - the Stocktwits news article on the Google Cloud AI release and the resulting 3% slide is at docs/61ddfe8b429fa05d4ddbc177c84432b69676ac6d.txt, indexed in snapshots/20260830T084004Z.json item 1, with entries dated 2026-08-26T04:36:16Z and 2026-08-22T01:08:24Z - so both the Workspace e-signature launch and the Cloud release were reported, headlined and dated a week or more before the print. Google entering e-signature is also a structural risk that has been on this name for years and appears in every DocuSign risk-factor section; a competitor's product launch that has been reported and traded is not new information three weeks later. What remains is a valuation assertion - that a terminal-value attack 'cannot be worth one 3% day' - with no dated source, no unit economics and no estimate of seat exposure, and it is the kind of claim that is unfalsifiable in either direction. The trendline and double-top corroboration is chart reading on the same bars. The 'no preview weighs the Google launch against the guide' argument is an n_queries=0 artefact of this capture.

findings.finding: Insider selling ran continuously into the print with no offsetting purchase: Form 144 and Form 4 both filed 2026-08-28 (four business days before the release), a 144 on 2026-08-07, Form 4s on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-04, and a nine-filing cluster of Form 4s and 144s on 2026-07-01 and 2026-07-10, spanning exactly the 16% rally.
findings.adversary_note: The hunter states the refutation itself: DocuSign insiders sell on standing plans every quarter, so the base rate is high and the marginal information is near zero. That is decisive and it is a size argument, not a publication argument - the filings are all in filings.json with dates, so they were reachable, but no body is stored and therefore not one share count or dollar value appears anywhere in this capture. Against a $12.18bn market cap and 3.16m shares a day of turnover, routine plan sales by executives are noise, and the July cluster of thirteen filings on 07-01 and 07-10 is exactly what scheduled post-print window openings look like at a company with broad equity compensation. A Form 4 also reports a completed transaction, so it describes supply already absorbed. I score it 32 rather than lower only because Form 144s genuinely are not surfaced by consumer aggregators and the capture does nothing to connect them.

A number that a public consensus aggregator displays on its own landing page for the ticker on the morning of the print is the definition of already out - the anchors put 'restates published consensus' at the top of the scale. The size is also negligible: $0.04 on EPS and $6.98m on revenue against a quarterly revenue base of the order of three-quarters of a billion dollars is under one percent, well inside the noise of a name whose median reaction is 7.64%. The hunter's own framing concedes most of this - it signs the finding against its other two, calls Estimize a small self-selected crowd, and notes the same crowd skews bullish when retail is long, which makes the datum a sentiment reading rather than an estimate edge.

findings.finding: An 8-K carrying only item 5.02 was accepted at 2026-08-28T20:18:17Z - Friday after the close, six days before the print - reporting an event dated 2026-08-26, accompanied within two hours by a Form 4 from a filer CIK (0002075006) that has no earlier filing in the 400-day index; this is the second 5.02-only 8-K in six weeks (the first was 2026-07-17), and neither appears in any of the 134 captured items outside the EDGAR index.
findings.adversary_note: The filings are reachable, so this cannot be scored low, but nothing about them is drawn out anywhere in the corpus and nothing about them is material to this print. Both accessions are in filings.json - 0001628280-26-059413 (8-K, item 5.02 only, accepted 2026-08-28T20:18:17Z) and the companion Form 4 0002075006-26-000006 - and the July 5.02 is in the same file, so any EDGAR reader had them six days ahead. That places this squarely in the reachable-but-unconnected band. What defeats the edge is size and mechanism rather than publication. Item 5.02 is the catch-all for director elections, officer appointments and compensatory arrangements, and a 5.02-only 8-K with a same-evening Form 4 from a brand-new filer CIK is the exact signature of a new director or officer receiving an initial grant - which is what a company mid-transition does routinely, not a buried resignation. The corroboration the hunter offers cuts against the finding: a Stocktwits user referring to a 'new CEO' on 2026-09-02 shows the transition was already common knowledge in the retail stream, so the transition is not the news. And even taken at its worst, a personnel change dated 2026-08-26 cannot alter the fiscal quarter that ended 2026-07-31; it can only affect commentary. The 'zero mentions across ninety Stocktwits messages' and n_queries=0 arguments are statements about the capture's query budget, not about market awareness.

findings.finding: Two Rule 144 notices of intent to sell were filed on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-27, into the strongest part of the 16% twenty-day rally and in the week before the print, with no offsetting insider purchase anywhere in the 400-day index.
findings.adversary_note: Both 144s are in filings.json with acceptance times, so they were reachable a week and two weeks before the print, and I agree no aggregator surfaces them - that is why this is 30 rather than 80. But this is the failure mode the brief warns hunters get wrong most often: it is real, low-visibility and far too small to matter. A Form 144 is a notice of intent to sell under a plan, the claim quotes no share count and no dollar value, and the capture stores no body for either, so there is no magnitude here at all - against a $2.34bn market cap and 4.64m shares a day of turnover, routine 10b5-1 executive sales in the weeks before a print are the base case at every software company and would need to be an order of magnitude larger than a typical 144 to register. The hunter's own independence note concedes this shares one source with #0 and should be collapsed into it, which means the two findings are one EDGAR-index observation, not two. And the supporting argument - 'if they were priced the run-in would not be +16%' - infers pricing from the run-up, which is not admissible here and would in any case be equally consistent with insiders selling into strength for tax or diversification reasons.
