findings.finding: An 8-K carrying items 5.02, 7.01 and 9.01 - a director or officer change plus a Reg FD disclosure and an attached exhibit - was filed on 2026-07-22 and is referenced in none of the 106 captured items; it is also the only 8-K between the last print and this one.
findings.adversary_note: The item codes defeat the finding. This 8-K carries item 7.01 - Regulation FD Disclosure - together with item 9.01, which means the company made a public disclosure and attached the document it disclosed. Regulation FD exists precisely to compel broad public dissemination; an issuer files under 7.01 when it has put information in front of the whole market, typically by press release. So the most likely state of the world is that Toro announced this on 2026-07-22 to everybody, and the reason it is absent from this corpus is that the capture ran no news search for this ticker (n_queries=0 in every admissible sweep) and stored a Stocktwits dump with two messages after 08-05. That is a capture artefact, not evidence the market did not see it, and I am instructed not to read it as a concession. I keep the score at the middle rather than higher only because the body is not stored, so I cannot confirm what was disclosed, and the finding is right that nothing in the corpus connects it to the print. Everything else about it is small: Toro is a 15.9% realised-vol industrial with a 3.02% median print reaction and a 1.51% deadband, and the tape shows no reaction whatsoever - run_up_20d +0.23% and the stock 2.56% off its 52-week high. The corroboration offered is a generic 'priced on margin expansion' analytic piece, which is true of most quality industrials and carries no size. The stated lean is 'slightly negative on the reaction base rate', which is a statement about history, not about this filing.

findings.finding: Lands' End's own FY26 guidance, issued at the 2026-06-09 print, is net revenue of $1.30-1.40bn, adjusted EBITDA of $68-78m and NET INCOME of $310-320m - the last figure being roughly the entire market value of the equity at $11.27 - because the WHP Global transaction monetised the Lands' End intellectual property, and the company simultaneously has a $100m share repurchase agreement in place, about 29% of the market capitalisation.
findings.adversary_note: Two things put this at the top of the scale. First, it restates published guidance: the $1.30-1.40bn revenue, $68-78m adjusted EBITDA and $310-320m net income figures and the $100m repurchase authorisation all come from the 2026-06-09 release, are in the stored body (docs/4b236ec1977fb78cc0d372d18adc6bc447a8957b.txt, snapshots/20260830T084126Z.json item 1, admissible per clean-view) and are in the 8-K items 2.02/7.01/9.01 in filings.json. Second, the finding's claim that 'nothing in the 88-item capture states it' is answered by its own independence field: Noble Capital Markets initiated coverage on 2026-06-18 with, in the hunter's words, 'precisely this thesis' - the WHP Global IP monetisation unlocking hidden brand value and the market underappreciating long-term earnings potential - published on channelchek. Published sell-side research asserting the exact conclusion is the strongest disproof of novelty available. Third, and most importantly, the arithmetic the finding calls unpriced is a category error. A $310-320m net income guide alongside a $68-78m adjusted EBITDA guide is a one-time, largely non-cash accounting gain from transferring the IP into the WHP structure - it is not distributable earnings and comparing it to a $365m market capitalisation as though the equity trades at 1.1x earnings is exactly the kind of arithmetic error the scale reserves its top band for. The operating business the market is capitalising is the $68-78m EBITDA line on declining revenue, which is precisely what the -41% from the high reflects. The buyback is real and large, but a $100m authorisation is an authorisation, not a completed retirement, and its existence has been public since June.

findings.finding: The last print behaved exactly the way a buyback-supported stock behaves: it opened down 5.8% pre-market on a revenue miss ('faces narrower loss but revenue miss on distribution disruption') and closed the session up 8.47% - a 14-point intraday reversal on 2026-06-09.
findings.adversary_note: The event is a June price bar, and price bars are the most public object in this exercise. The close-to-close +8.47% is in the sealed baseline's own history, and the pre-market -5.8% is quoted in the admissible stored body (entry 2026-06-09T12:29:17Z) - so both halves are published, one in the baseline and one in the capture. The claim that the join 'is exactly the kind of two-source join nothing publishes' overstates the difficulty: a fourteen-point intraday reversal on the day of a results release is visible on any intraday chart of 2026-06-09 and is the sort of session that gets narrated in real time by the same stream the hunter is reading. The inference - that the marginal buyer at this price is not reacting to the revenue line - is one observation from one session three months ago, and the finding itself asks to have it collapsed into #0. There is also a sequencing problem: whatever the buyback did on 06-09, the stock is 11.9% lower over the last twenty sessions and 7.5% lower over the last five, so if a price-insensitive repurchase bid were the dominant force it is not visible in the recent tape.

findings.finding: A management-transition cluster sits in July: 8-Ks with item 5.02 on 2026-06-30 and again on 2026-07-10, an S-8 registration on 2026-07-14, a Form 3 and a Form 4 on 2026-07-15, and a Form 144 on 2026-07-23 - two officer or director changes eleven days apart followed immediately by a new-insider equity registration.
findings.adversary_note: This is the reachable-but-unconnected case and I score it there. Every accession is in filings.json with a date - two 8-Ks carrying item 5.02 on 06-30 and 07-10, an S-8 on 07-14, a Form 3 and Form 4 on 07-15, a 144 on 07-23 and two Form 4s on 08-04 - so an EDGAR reader had the whole sequence six weeks out, but no body is stored and nothing in the capture draws it together. What stops it going lower is exactly that quietness; what stops it going higher is that the sequence has an entirely ordinary reading. An 8-K item 5.02, followed four days later by an S-8 and then by a Form 3 from a new filer, is the standard paperwork of hiring an officer and registering the shares for their equity plan - the S-8 is the tell, because a departure does not require a new registration statement. Two 5.02 filings eleven days apart at a company mid-restructuring is unremarkable when one of them is plausibly a board change. The finding provides no name, no role and no size, and it correctly signs itself against the other two. Its own framing - 'the main thing that could make the guide unreliable' - is a conditional about a possibility, not a fact about the quarter.

findings.finding: The whole print reduces to one number that the market has already assumed favourably: at the 2026-05-26 release management gave an early FY27 framework of roughly 16-17% ARR and revenue growth, down from about 25%, and the stock fell more than 31% - 'now September 3 arrives with that same 16%-17% growth framework still sitting in plain sight... management either firms that number up and gives investors a reason it was a floor, or confirms the slowdown just as the stock has recovered off the June lows', with the explicit invalidator being 'a reiteration of 16%-17% with no upward qualifier, or any further commentary on go-to-market disruption'.
findings.adversary_note: The underlying fact is published guidance and the interpretation is a published document, and the one option reading I am permitted on this name contradicts the conclusion. The 16-17% FY27 ARR and revenue framework was given by management at the 2026-05-26 release; the market's response is the largest reaction in the baseline history at -31.52%. Guidance that caused a 31% de-rating is not information the market has failed to absorb. The framing the finding presents as its edge - guide-floor binary, the invalidator being a reiteration with no upward qualifier - is not the hunter's construction either; it is quoted verbatim from docs/c93e70fe3290d74cd85541bdbc523d17e1e60435.txt, a post published at wp.optionbeast.com on 2026-08-29 and captured in snapshots/20260902T154652Z.json item 15, i.e. publicly on the web five days before the print. The finding even quotes that document making its central claim for it. Most importantly, this is one of only two names in this day's corpus where a genuine pre-print implied move survives, and it refutes the positioning argument. The same document records an implied move of about 13% quoted from Bloomberg, against a 9.79% historical median: the option market is pricing a move a third larger than history, which is the opposite of a market 'not positioned' for a bad outcome. A 13% straddle on a stock 47% below its 52-week high is a market braced for exactly the reiteration scenario the finding says is unanticipated. What is genuinely true here is that the 9.35% twenty-session rally raises the bar - but that is the run-up, it is in the baseline, and it is not an unpriced fact.

findings.finding: The security complex has just demonstrated that good numbers get sold: 'Palo Alto Sinks 8% Despite 34% Revenue Growth, CrowdStrike Falls 3%, Fortinet Slips' - and Zscaler rallied 9.35% over the twenty sessions into its own print on the back of that same peer reporting season.
findings.adversary_note: Every peer print in the list was a major, separately reported market event, and the capture stores two independent write-ups of the pattern in the same sweep - the headline item at snapshots/20260902T154652Z.json item 24 and the optionbeast document, which records Palo Alto falling about 8% despite 34% growth and CrowdStrike falling roughly 4% in sympathy. The 'pattern is not aggregated' claim fails on its own evidence: two publishers in one capture aggregating the same set is aggregation. And the price has already answered it. Zscaler rallied 9.35% over the twenty sessions containing that peer reporting season - the market watched PANW get sold on 34% growth and bought Zscaler anyway, which is a considered response, not an oversight. The finding's own line, 'Zscaler's own tape moved the opposite way to the lesson', is the concession. The multiple argument that follows is the weakest part and the hunter says so: it cites a 'Cybersecurity Valuation Multiples 2026' piece in the same sweep and then admits no number was extracted from it, so the claim that Zscaler is the highest-multiple, slowest-guided name in the group is asserted rather than shown anywhere in this corpus.

findings.finding: Zscaler systematically breaks its implied move and has broken it to the downside twice at this point in the calendar: options priced about 13% before 2026-05-26 and the stock fell more than 31%; they priced 10.6% before 2026-09-03 in 2024 and it fell 20.6%; across the last eight prints it has exceeded the implied move five times. The implied move for this print is again about 13%.
findings.adversary_note: This is a published options statistic drawn from a published document, and it is the sort of number that free earnings-option sites put on their landing page for every ticker. It comes from the same optionbeast post (line 454) as #0, which the hunter says should be collapsed into one cluster, and the finding is explicitly a magnitude observation with a two-sided tail and no directional content - the same statistic 'shows upside breaks too', as it says. The historical implied-versus-realised record for a liquid optionable name is exactly what marketchameleon, whose page is captured in the same sweep as item 24, exists to publish. There is also a partial internal answer to the finding: it argues that the ~13% implied and the 9.79% median both understate the distribution, but the 13% implied is already a third above the median, which is the option market having widened for precisely the reason the finding gives. Five breaks in eight is also not far from what one would expect when the implied move is a straddle-derived expectation rather than a bound.

findings.finding: On the evening of 2026-09-01, hours before this before-the-open print, CollPlant announced a 1-for-10 reverse share split to take effect at the Nasdaq open on 2026-09-04 - the session immediately AFTER the print - explicitly 'as part of the Company's strategic plan to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement for continued listing'.
findings.adversary_note: This is wire copy in the capture. The reverse split went out on PR Newswire on 2026-09-01 and is stored as a body (docs/ee32750e276846aba37596bed7e3b23135338ee9.txt) and indexed in snapshots/20260902T150801Z.json item 1, with the company's own 6-K in filings.json (accession 0001213900-26-096233, accepted 2026-09-01T20:30:01Z). A press release plus a same-evening 6-K is the maximum publication a nano-cap can achieve; there is nothing left for the market to learn. The interpretation - that a compliance reverse split says the company does not expect the price to recover on its own - is a truism about every reverse split ever announced, and a 1-for-10 is mechanically value-neutral. The corroboration offered is a second Stocktwits post in the very same stored document reading the sequence identically, which is publication, not independence. I also checked the tape, and the market repriced immediately: quote.json shows 0.388 on 08-31 falling to 0.373 on 09-01 and the baseline's completed 09-02 close at 0.343 (split-adjusted 3.43), i.e. -11.6% over the two sessions spanning the announcement. The claim that it cannot be priced because 'the stock would not have been bid 25% higher two sessions earlier on a pivot headline' compares the reaction to a different piece of news on a different day and does not survive contact with the intervening bars. Finally, the mechanism partly misses the print: the split takes effect at the 09-04 open, after the release, so its own price effect is a scheduled mechanical adjustment, not a print outcome.

findings.finding: Two sessions before the print, on 2026-08-31, CollPlant announced it was acquiring LightSolver and entering the photonic-computing and supercomputing markets - consideration paid in newly issued shares AND warrants - and the stock traded 182,733,300 shares against a float the corpus puts at 13.0-13.5m, halted up, ran roughly 35% intraday, and closed only 8.4% higher before giving it all back over the next two sessions.
findings.adversary_note: The acquisition is a 6-K plus a snapshot item and the finding concedes the headline is priced. What is left - the shape of the flow - is quote.json, the one file that is by construction public. I verified the arithmetic and it holds on an unadjusted basis: quote.json's 2026-08-31 bar is 182,733,300 shares at a 0.388 close, which against a 13.0-13.5m float is roughly thirteen turns, and the market cap of $5.48m at that price implies about 16m shares out, so the ratio is real rather than a units error. But that is precisely why it is priced: a nano-cap that turns thirteen times its float in one session, halts up, runs 35% and closes only 8.4% higher has been repriced in public, in the most visible way a stock can be, and the round-trip over the following two sessions (0.388 to 0.373 to 0.343) is the market completing that judgement before the print. The finding's own conclusion - distribution into retail - is the market's verdict on the pivot, not information withheld from it. One caution on the numbers the hunter and I are both using: quote.json here is unadjusted for the 1-for-10 split while the baseline is adjusted, and the 09-02 bar in quote.json (0.3097, 1,299,693 shares, fetched 2026-09-02T15:08:01Z) is a partial intraday bar - a reader who mixed the two series would be out by a factor of ten. The dilution machinery in the independence field (F-1, F-3, 424B3/B5, two Form Ds) is all in filings.json and all months old; age is not novelty.

findings.finding: Three SCHEDULE 13D/A amendments were filed in twenty-five days - 2026-07-27, 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-21 - in a company whose float the corpus puts at 13.0-13.5m shares, immediately after a Form D private placement (2026-07-20) and a resale prospectus going effective (424B3, 2026-07-17).
findings.adversary_note: The three 13D/A accessions are in filings.json with dates, so they were reachable, but nothing in the capture draws out who filed them, for how many shares, or in which direction - the bodies are not stored and the hunter says so. That is the reachable-but-unconnected band and I will not score it higher. What caps it is size and mechanism rather than publication. This is a $5.5m market cap; a >5% holder's position moving 'materially' is a few hundred thousand dollars, and against a session in which 182.7m shares changed hands the supply implication of three amendments is not measurable. A 13D/A also reports a position change that has already occurred, so it describes flow behind the tape, not in front of it, and the last of the three is dated 2026-08-21, before the 08-31 volume event that would have absorbed any of it. The finding correctly says this collapses into the same EDGAR-index cluster as #1, so it is not a second observation.

findings.finding: Insiders sold into the melt-up: Form 144 notices on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19 with Form 4s on 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19 - three intents-to-sell inside seven days - during exactly the run that took the stock 30.1% higher over twenty sessions to within 5.5% of its 52-week high, and there is no offsetting purchase anywhere in the index.
findings.adversary_note: The filings are reachable and genuinely unaggregated, so this belongs in the 20-40 band, but it dies on size. Not one share count or dollar value appears anywhere in this capture for any of the three 144s or two Form 4s - no body is stored - and the company trades 66,237,575 shares a day on a $9.50bn market cap. For insider intents-to-sell to be informative against that, they would have to be a multiple of a day's volume, and typical executive plan sales at a company of this size are a rounding error on a single session. Three 144s inside seven days is also the signature of a scheduled window opening after a blackout, which at a name reporting in early September means the mid-August window - exactly where these sit. The finding's affirmative argument is the one I am instructed not to accept: 'if the market had priced insiders exiting into the rally, the run-in would not be +30%'. That is the run-up standing in for an option reading, and the hunter concedes half of it by noting the 30.1% and the volume figure come from the baseline tape rather than from any document. The retail stream's failure to mention insider selling is not evidence about the marginal price-setter in a stock with 66m shares of daily institutional turnover.

findings.finding: The print is arriving with the bar reset upward on the day itself: Needham raised its price target to $22.00 on the morning of 2026-09-03, the Estimize crowd sits $0.03 above Wall Street on EPS and $8.48m above on revenue, and a corpus item states 'institutional desks are monitoring this print with high intent to see if their new Agentic AI layer can drive a massive ARR beat' - so the requirement is an ARR acceleration, not a beat.
findings.adversary_note: The hunter says 'this is mostly priced' and it is right - every component is published, and published on the morning of the print in the same admissible sweep. The Needham target raise to $22.00 is a gurufocus news item captured at 15:08Z (docs/94ca8769ddaff2dce7685a3314d1bc4d7ac00ae3.txt, entries 2026-09-03T14:26:58Z and 14:26:28Z); the Estimize spread is a free public consensus page, the same source I judged as published for DOCU; and the 26% short-interest figure is itself in the captured stream at the 13:30:55Z entry. A broker target published hours before the release is the most visible form of expectation setting there is, and 'expectation stacking' is an interpretation of that published material, not a fact beyond it. The size is also small: $0.03 on EPS and $8.48m on revenue is well under one percent of a quarterly revenue base at this company's scale, and the 'institutional desks are monitoring this print with high intent' quote is unattributed promotional copy with no informational content. The one genuinely useful thing here is what the hunter flags itself: the 26% short interest points the other way, so the finding's own two halves cancel, which is why it declines to size it and why the band crosses zero.

findings.finding: This is the first results release under a CFO who started one month earlier: Jonathan Collins was announced on 2026-06-29 effective 2026-08-03 at a $550k base, his Form 3 was filed 2026-08-04, and three days later an 8-K with items 5.02/7.01/9.01 moved senior VP Parag Desai to part-time with retirement in October 2026 and a consulting role - a finance and senior-management turnover cluster inside the four weeks before the print.
findings.adversary_note: The CFO change is published in this capture, dated, and two months old. The appointment of Jonathan Collins was announced on 2026-06-29 and appears in the stored body docs/4f5b168d5df0737fa55ae98ce2a74c43b91e324c.txt at the 2026-06-29T11:03:17Z entry, with the 08-06 8-K at 2026-08-06T11:03:16Z in the same document, and the Form 3, Form 4 and the items 5.02/7.01/9.01 8-K are all in filings.json. A CFO start date, a base salary and a senior VP's phased retirement are exactly the facts an 8-K exists to publish, and the market had nine weeks with them. What is left is a behavioural heuristic - a new CFO's first print is the moment to rebase guidance or take a writedown - which is generic, applies to every CFO transition at every company, carries no size, and is unsupported by any dated source in the capture. It is also a claim about the shape of a possible disclosure rather than about the quarter, so its sign is indeterminate: a rebase can as easily reset the bar low and be bought. The corroboration is weaker than presented: a 13D/A accepted on 2026-08-03 is a holder's report of a completed change, its body is not stored, no holder is named and no stake size is given, and the coincidence with a start date is a coincidence of a five-business-day window. Note also that the 07-22 8-K item 5.07 the finding elsewhere relies on is itself the public record of the meeting outcome, so the sequence it describes was fully assembled on EDGAR.

findings.finding: A proxy fight ran to a vote in July and the board won it: an activist publicly demanded the resignation of director Joanna Barsh over a misleading bio on 2026-07-01, the company recommended FOR all nine directors citing ISS support on 2026-07-07, DEFA14A supplements were filed 2026-07-09 and 2026-07-13, and the meeting results were filed as an 8-K item 5.07 on 2026-07-22 - after which the activist filed a 13D/A on 2026-08-03.
findings.adversary_note: A proxy contest is the single most heavily published corporate event there is, and this capture proves it: the activist's public demand for a director's resignation is in the stored body at 2026-07-01T23:50:18Z, the company's FOR-all-nine recommendation citing ISS support is at 2026-07-07T19:13:01Z, and the DEFA14A supplements of 07-09 and 07-13, the 8-K item 5.07 of 07-22 and the 13D/A of 08-03 are all in filings.json (docs/4f5b168d5df0737fa55ae98ce2a74c43b91e324c.txt, admissible snapshots per clean-view). Proxy solicitation material is mailed to every holder by law and ISS recommendations are distributed to the entire institutional base - there is no plausible sense in which a resolved July proxy fight is unpriced information in September. The finding's own claim that 'nothing in the capture reports the vote outcome' is answered by the filing it cites in the same sentence: an 8-K item 5.07 is the vote outcome. The residual - that a shareholder base which just voted on the strategy will read this print differently - is a statement about how the reaction might be shaped, not about a fact the market lacks, and it has no size. And the closing argument, that a 14.6% twenty-session decline 'is not what a market pricing an activist-supported turnaround looks like', is the baseline's own run_up_20d field used as evidence against itself: that decline is the pricing.

findings.finding: An 8-K carrying ONLY item 8.01 (Other Events) was filed on 2026-08-13, three weeks before the print, and it is referenced nowhere in the 22-item pre-print news sweep, nowhere in the 150-item first sweep, and nowhere in the social stream - a standalone Other Events filing at a company three weeks from results is either a strategic announcement, a settlement or a disclosure the company wanted separated from the earnings release.
findings.adversary_note: This is reachable-but-unconnected and I keep it in that band, but with a caveat that cuts harder here than at any other name on this day. The 8-K is in filings.json with an item code and a date, so it was public three weeks before the print; the body is not stored, so nobody - hunter or adversary - knows what it says, and a finding whose content is unknown cannot carry a sign. The hunter concedes that. The caveat is the coverage asymmetry: LULU is one of only four tickers in this whole capture that carries real news items, and the capture ran a 22-query news sweep on the morning of the print plus a 150-item first sweep, and neither surfaced any August company announcement. For a $12.5bn household-name consumer stock, that is weak but genuine evidence of immateriality rather than of a missed disclosure - a material standalone 8-K at this company would be reported, unlike at the twenty-nine names in this run where n_queries=0 makes silence uninformative. Item 8.01 is also the catch-all used for entirely routine things: setting an earnings date, a debt or buyback authorisation, an investor-day notice, a legal-proceedings update with no financial effect. The 13D/A bracketing adds nothing without a holder name or a stake size, both absent.

findings.finding: The founder's proxy campaign appears to have changed the board: a PREC14A nominated Laura Gentile, Eric Hirshberg and Marc Maurer as Class I directors on a GOLD universal proxy card, the 2026 annual meeting produced an 8-K carrying items 5.02 AND 5.07 on 2026-06-26, and three days later on 2026-06-29 two Form 3s and eleven Form 4s were filed at once - i.e. new insiders seated on the board immediately after the vote.
findings.adversary_note: The proxy contest, its resolution and the CEO succession are all published, and the finding half-admits it ('the proxy fight was covered'). A PREC14A is mailed to every holder; a DEFA14A of 2026-06-05 is in filings.json; an 8-K carrying item 5.07 on 2026-06-26 is the certified record of the vote, publicly filed; and the leadership half - Calvin McDonald's departure announced on the December 2025 call and Heidi O'Neill's appointment being read as a vote of no confidence - is in the captured coverage (tradingkey piece, cited in the brief's own independence field, and docs/a6714b8a9efb77fcb23338c7664926c08439b598.txt from snapshots/20260903T151408Z.json item 19). A founder-led proxy campaign at a company of this profile is among the most covered governance events of the year; the notion that its outcome went unreported is not credible and the finding's evidence for it is the absence of a headline in a 22-query sweep. I also think the filing pattern is misread. Two Form 3s and eleven Form 4s all dated 2026-06-29, three days after an annual meeting, is the ordinary annual-meeting mechanic: directors receive their annual equity grant immediately after the AGM, which produces a Form 4 for every continuing director, while a Form 3 is filed only by genuinely new insiders. Eleven Form 4s therefore indicate eleven existing insiders being granted, not eleven new ones seated - the count of new arrivals is two. That materially weakens 'a reconstituted board'. What remains is the kitchen-sink heuristic - new board plus new CEO equals reset quarter - which is generic, unsized and undated, and its sign is not even stable, since a reset can clear the decks and be bought.

findings.finding: The fundamentals going into the reset are already deteriorating on the company's own numbers: the corpus captures 'Lululemon cuts 2026 forecast as sales slump across Americas', a separate analysis titled 'Lululemon Q1 FY2026: The Brand Is Still There. The Business Has Fractured.', and a China-specific piece noting the China engine 'just hit a wall' with the stock down 46% in 2026.
findings.adversary_note: The hunter says it outright: 'this is the consensus narrative and overlaps with everything else in the sweep', and 'largely priced - a 43.6% drawdown from the high says so'. I agree and the scale puts consensus-in-the-captured-coverage at 90-100. Every element is a published headline in the pre-print sweep - 'Lululemon cuts 2026 forecast as sales slump across Americas', 'Lululemon Q1 FY2026: The Brand Is Still There. The Business Has Fractured.', and the tikr China piece which prints the -46% year-to-date figure in its own headline (snapshots/20260903T151408Z.json items 5, 7, 9 and 22). The guidance cut is the company's own disclosure from the June print, which the baseline records as an -8.56% reaction. There is no arithmetic here that has not been performed in public, repeatedly, by named outlets, in documents this capture stores.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-01, two days before the results print, Amber International announced it was abandoning its 'Amber Premium' digital-asset wealth identity and rebranding to AMBR as an 'agentic AI company', launching AI agents Ambre and MIA - a total repositioning of the business released at 3:30 AM ET on PR Newswire, immediately ahead of the numbers.
findings.adversary_note: The rebrand is in the capture as a stored body and as a snapshot item (docs/6b85260769557edb0697f5f8fb5e6b9aced19f03.txt, snapshots/20260901T150802Z.json item 1) and as a company filing in filings.json (6-K 0001104659-26-103605, accepted 2026-08-31T09:21:07Z), and quote.json shows the market pricing it in the single largest bar in the whole series: 2026-09-01 traded 15,889,900 shares against 19k-56k in the preceding week and closed at 0.88, down 24% from the prior close of 1.16 after an opening pop. The market did not take the pivot as good news - it sold it by a quarter in one session. The hunter's residual is therefore not the announcement but a behavioural prior, that a sub-$100m issuer discarding its brand 48 hours before results is pre-framing bad numbers, and no document in this capture asserts that, dates it, or sizes it. Two further problems. First, 'nobody connected them' rests on n_queries=0 in every sweep, which is a statement about the capture's query budget, not about what the market saw; the instructions are explicit that this is neither concession nor publication. Second, the claim that the market failed to connect the two is directly contradicted by the bar it cites: a stock marked down 24% on 300x volume on the announcement day has connected something.

findings.finding: quote.json shows 15,889,900 shares traded on 2026-09-01 against a 20-day average near 1.09m and a late-August run of 19k-55k a day - roughly 29% of the ~55m float turning over in one session, with the close at 0.88 after an intraday high well above 1.40, i.e. a complete distribution of the pivot rally into the print.
findings.adversary_note: This finding's entire evidence base is quote.json, which is to say it is the price. A 15.9m-share bar closing at the low of the day is not information the market lacks; it is the market's own footprint, visible to every participant on every chart, and the hunter's own corpus_ref is the bar itself rather than any document. Worse, the reading is contradicted by the next bar. The claim describes 'a complete distribution of the pivot rally into the print' with 'the close at 0.88', but 0.88 is the 09-01 close, and the baseline's last_close_date 2026-09-02 spot is 1.02 - the stock rose about 16% off 0.88 on the session after the alleged distribution, which is the opposite of a name being liquidated into a print. The quote.json 09-02 bar (0.95 on 3,919,986 shares, fetched 2026-09-02T15:08:55Z) is a partial intraday bar and appears to be what the claim read as the state of play. The Nasdaq minimum-bid leg is also mechanically wrong: compliance requires 30 consecutive business days below $1.00, and the corpus shows only four scattered sub-$1 closes (08-19, 08-20, 08-21, 09-01) with the stock back at 1.02 pre-print, so no deficiency clock the claim implies can have started. The Stocktwits 30,000-share short anecdote is one retail post and cannot corroborate a float-turnover claim.

findings.finding: An 8-K with items 5.02 and 9.01 - a director or officer change announced with a press release - was filed on 2026-08-20, inside the window in which the stock fell from $102 to $83 in seven business days, and it is mentioned in none of the 83 captured items; the admissible social stream on 2026-08-18 records only '102 to 83 in 7 business days, wow. No bounce' with no cause given.
findings.adversary_note: Two things hold this at the midpoint. First, the item codes say it was announced: an 8-K carrying item 5.02 with item 9.01 means an exhibit was furnished, which for a management change is a press release, so the company put it on a wire. Victoria's Secret is a $7.1bn consumer name that trades 1.5m shares a day and is covered by every retail-sector desk; a management change there is reported the same morning. The reason it is absent from this corpus is that no news search was run for this ticker and the stored stream is retail brand banter - a capture artefact, not evidence the market missed it. Second, the chronology in the finding does not hold. It says the 8-K sits 'inside the window in which the stock fell from $102 to $83 in seven business days', but the corpus quote recording that fall is dated 2026-08-18T18:42:03Z, two days BEFORE the 2026-08-20 filing - so the 19% drawdown was already complete when the 8-K was filed and cannot have been caused by it, nor can the 8-K be the unexplained cause the finding is looking for. What is left is an unread item code with no direction: 5.02 covers appointments and compensatory arrangements as readily as departures, no body is stored, and the stated lean ('departures get filed before results') is an unsourced base-rate assertion. The 13D/A of 07-29 adds an unnamed holder with an unstated stake.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is extended and the sell-side is behind it: the stock is 269% above its 52-week low after a +47.44% reaction to the previous print, UBS's raised target of $95 (from $90, 2026-08-18) is only 12% above the pre-print price, another corpus item puts the 'latest analyst PT' at $80 - below the market - and participants describe high short interest and a squeeze dynamic rather than a fundamental bid.
findings.adversary_note: The hunter concedes the components are 'individually all wire copy' and the capture confirms every one of them. UBS's raise to $95 from $90 on 2026-08-18, the second house's $80 mark, and the short-interest and squeeze discussion are all in the stored body at entries dated 2026-08-18T16:31:02Z, 2026-08-25T12:23:08Z and 2026-08-26T15:57:38Z (docs/621d0cd2f2ce628fcfa8161af1d684a409ae43e9.txt, admissible snapshots). The remaining two facts - the stock is 269% above its 52-week low and the prior print produced +47.44% - are fields in the sealed baseline, which is to say the market's own record of what it has already done. Combining published targets with a published price to observe that the stock trades above the sell-side's marks is subtraction on public numbers, and it is a permanent condition of any stock that has tripled: targets lag price by construction, in every squeeze, always. That is structural, not novel. The mechanism is also self-cancelling in the way the finding admits: 'a print that merely meets expectations removes the squeeze fuel' and 'a genuine short base can be squeezed further' are the two halves of a coin, and nothing in the capture gives a short-interest figure from an exchange source to weight them.

findings.finding: An 8-K with items 5.02 and 9.01 was filed on 2026-08-28, six days before the fiscal-year-end print - a director or officer change accompanied by an exhibit, i.e. announced by press release - and it is referenced in none of the 38 captured items; it follows a SCHEDULE 13D/A on 2026-06-26 and a Reg FD 8-K (items 7.01, 9.01) on 2026-06-17.
findings.adversary_note: The filing is reachable and its circulation in this capture is genuinely nil, so it sits in the reachable-but-unconnected band - but one detail in the finding's own description pushes it toward the top of that band rather than the bottom. The 8-K carries item 9.01, which means an exhibit was furnished, and the finding correctly reads that as a press release. A company that issues a press release has distributed the news on a wire to every subscriber; the fact that this capture ran no news search (n_queries=0 in every sweep) and stored only a Stocktwits dump is why the announcement is invisible here, and that is a capture artefact rather than evidence the market did not see it. So the most likely state of the world is that the change was publicly announced on 2026-08-28 and simply is not in this corpus. Beyond that, the finding cannot carry a sign: no body is stored, item 5.02 covers appointments as readily as departures, and the hunter's stated basis for leaning negative - 'companies time departures to just before a results release rather than just after' - is a base-rate assertion with no source and no obvious truth to it. The 13D/A of 06-26 and the Reg FD 8-K of 06-17 are further unread item codes. At a $207m issuer with 70,415 shares a day of volume, this is also a name where the print itself carries a 14.05% median reaction, so an unquantified governance item is small relative to the event it precedes.

findings.finding: The results are already out: Galmed filed two 6-Ks on 2026-09-02 reporting interim results for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 with a net loss of $2.7m, and the earliest admissible post-release reaction in the capture describes it as 'very disappointing... today after 1 year, ended up in confused out of focus and back to early stage bio company. No cash partnerships, dumping its own late stage assets & starting fresh and again expected delays' - so the 2026-09-03 calendar row is stale and what is left to trade is drift on a strategic reset, not a fresh surprise.
findings.adversary_note: I agree with the finding's premise and that is exactly why it scores near the top of the scale: there was no distinct earnings event on 2026-09-03 for this name. Two 6-Ks reporting the quarter ended 30 June 2026 were filed on 2026-09-02 (filings.json), the baseline's event_plausibility is 'unknown' with cadence_implausible and last_print 2026-09-02 one day earlier, and the reaction is already in the bars the baseline seals - the history records the 09-02 event at -4.83%, and run_up_5d is -8.96% with run_up_20d -18.20% into a 09-03 close of 3.92. Once the release is out and the market has traded two sessions on it, the results are the price by definition; a claim whose own headline is 'the results are already out' cannot also be an unpriced fact. What the finding actually asserts is drift - that an illiquid nano-cap takes several days to re-rate a strategy reversal - and that is a momentum hypothesis, not information, with no dated source and no size. There is also a methodological problem with its evidence that I have to flag, because it follows from the finding's own dating: if the release was made on 09-02, then snapshots/20260903T150908Z.json is post-release material and the quote it leans on ('very disappointing... today after 1 year, ended up in confused out of focus...') is post-print reaction commentary, not pre-print evidence. The hunter labels that snapshot admissible on the basis of the tagged after-the-close 09-03 session while simultaneously arguing the release preceded it; those two positions cannot both hold. Finally, the closing argument - 'if it were priced the stock would not have needed a 1-for-8 reverse split three weeks ago' - is a non sequitur: the split was a listing mechanic completed on 08-19 and says nothing about whether the September results are in the price.

findings.finding: A POS AM (post-effective amendment) was filed on 2026-09-02, the same day as the results, on top of 424B3 prospectuses dated 2026-06-08 and 2026-06-22 and a POS EX on 2026-06-08 - and retail participants independently observed the company selling stock at the market on 2026-08-24 ('looks like they ATM'ing', 'I was thinking that the CEO was using Galmed as an ATM') - in a share that has just been reverse-split 1-for-8 on 2026-08-19 and sits 4.5% above its 52-week low.
findings.adversary_note: This is the better of the two and I put it in the middle rather than the refuted band, but two things hold it there. First, it is half published already: the at-the-market selling the finding treats as its discovery is being narrated in the captured stream by retail participants on 2026-08-24 ('looks like they ATM'ing', 'I was thinking that the CEO was using Galmed as an ATM', docs/8c2c7f33148bf6712100e164894cff256da07b40.txt), and the 424B3 prospectuses of 06-08 and 06-22 plus the POS EX are all in filings.json, so the supply mechanism is both reachable and being discussed.
